title: Insurance Virtual Assistant + Appointment Setter — US Health & Life Agency (Long-Term, $800-$1,000/mo)
job_title: Insurance Virtual Assistant + Appointment Setter — US Health & Life Agency (Long-Term, $800-$1,000/mo)
description: Lead generation, appointment setting, and documentation for a US-based licensed insurance agent. Long-term seat, full-time, US night shift from Manila. ($800-$1,000/mo) Read this whole post before you apply. I auto-delete applications that skip the steps at the bottom. I'm a US-based licensed health and life insurance agent in Tampa, Florida. I run my own agency. I'm hiring ONE long-term virtual assistant and appointment setter to become my right hand. I'm not hiring for a month. I'm hiring someone I'll build with for years. I generate more hot leads every week than I can call alone. Right now most of them go cold because I'm one person. That ends when I hire you. Your job is to call my leads, qualify them, and book them onto my calendar so I can do what I do best — talk to people who are ready to buy. You will NOT sell anything. You will NOT quote prices. You will NOT explain insurance plans. I am the licensed advisor and I handle all of that. Your job is the phone, the booking, the notes, and the follow-up. Everything that happens before I get on the call is on you. What you'll do every shift 1. Call my "yes" leads — people who already said they want coverage. You call the newest ones first. 2. Call new leads within 5 minutes of them landing in my system. 3. Call older leads that have gone cold and re-open them. 4. Run my discovery script on every call. I give you the exact words. 5. Qualify the lead with a few simple questions, then book them onto my Google Calendar. 6. Look up a lead's public options on a free public website before I call, and drop your notes into my system. 7. Send follow-up text messages and leave voi cemail s on people who don't pick up. 8. Update my CRM (Podio) and my dialer (Ringy) after every single call. 9. Keep my lead tracker, pipeline tracker, and revenue tracker spreadsheets current. 10. Send confirmation texts to everyone scheduled for the day. 11. Work the no-answer pile every shift — at least 10 attempts before a lead is marked dead. 12. Send me an end-of-shift report so it's waiting in my inbox when I wake up. What you will NEVER do - You never quote a rate or a price. - You never pitch or explain a product. - You never answer "how much does it cost" — you book the appointment instead. - You never ask about someone's health, medications, or conditions over text. Phone only. - You never use the words "guaranteed," "best," or "cheapest." I train you on the exact handoff line for every one of these. It's simple and you'll have it memorized in your first week. The phone setup — no personal phone needed You dial through my software using my logins, from your browser. My US phone number shows up on the caller ID, so every prospect thinks they're getting a call from the States. All calls record under my account. You need a stable computer, a USB headset, and reliable internet. That's it. No personal phone, no SIM card, no phone bill. The two tools you'll dial through are Sales God (my main dialer) and Ringy (my CRM dialer). Browser-based, both of them. If you've used Five9, Aircall, JustCall, Mojo, CallTools, or Ringy before, you'll feel at home fast. The English standard — this is the #1 thing I screen for My prospects are American. When you call them, they cannot be able to tell you're not calling from inside the US. Your accent has to be clean and neutral. This is the single most important requirement in this post. If your spoken English has a heavy accent, this role isn't the right fit — and the voice recording step below is exactly how I check. I'm not being unkind about it. I'm being clear so you don't spend time applying for something that won't match. Plenty of Filipino VAs have a neutral, American-sounding phone voice. If that's you, I want to talk. The schedule - Monday to Friday, 10 AM to 7 PM Eastern Standard Time. - That's 10 PM to 7 AM Manila time. - Full-time, 40 hours a week. - You must already have experience working the US night shift from the Philippines. If you've never done graveyard shift for a US client, this will be a rough fit and I'll know within a week. The pay - Base pay is $800 to $1,000 USD per month, depending on your experience and how the trial week goes. - Paid weekly through Wise. - Performance bonuses may be available after proven long-term performance is demonstrated. I reward people who earn it over time. I don't promise bonus money on day one. Who I'm looking for - 1+ year of solid history on OnlineJobs.ph with real reviews. - Prior phone experience with a US company — insurance, real estate, SaaS, or call-center appointment setting. - Experience dialing through a browser-based system tied to a client's account. - A neutral, American-sounding phone voice. - Someone who wants ONE long-term home, not five clients at once. If you're juggling multiple clients, we're not a fit. I want your focus. - Reliable, self-managing, and honest. I have to trust your reports. How to apply — three steps. Skip one and I delete it. I'm going to get a lot of applications. These three steps tell me who actually reads and follows instructions. That's the job, so this is the test. 1. Use this exact subject line: **Tampa Setter** (If your subject line is anything else, I won't open it.) 2. Record a 60-second voice clip on ---------- reading the short script below out loud, exactly as written. Paste the Vocaroo link in your application. This is how I judge your phone voice, so record it like you're actually on a call — warm, clear, confident. 3. In two or three sentences, tell me: the longest US night-shift role you've held, and what browser dialers/CRM tools you've used. Be specific. Name the tools. The script to read for your voice recording > "Hi, is this [first name]? Hey [first name], this is Heather. You recently responded yes to a text from us about exploring your health coverage options — is that right? Awesome. I'm not here to sell you anything or quote you a price on this call. My only job is to ask you a couple quick questions and get you booked with my senior advisor Ryan, who walks you through the actual details. Do you have just two minutes for me right now?" That's it. Subject line, voice clip, two-sentence note. Applications that follow all three steps go to the top of my list. I read every complete application personally. If you're the right person, this is a stable, long-term seat with an owner who'll invest in you. I'm looking forward to hearing your voice. — Ryan Kucks, Kucks Health LLC, Tampa FL

Act as a direct buffer for the owner by monitoring milestone dates, checking boards for data entry holes, and cleanly requesting real-time updates from other tea ---------- mbers inside the platform. Technical Literacy: Advanced experience with Microsoft Outlook (specifically multi-account structures, folder logic). Highly comfortable with or capable of instantly navigating project management infrastructure like OpenProject, Asana, or Basecamp. Communication: Exceptional written English and clear, text-based asynchronous communication. You must be comfortable tracking down task details independently. 4. Expectations & Work Culture Engagement Type: Part-time (3 hours per week). Culture Fit: Guided by classical principles of stewardship, progress, and systematic order. Mistakes are never fixed *for* you; instead, the owner will point out errors so you can systematically correct them yourself to master the process. 5. title: Executive Support Specialist

The Mindset We’re Looking For The best Executive Support Specialists we’ve worked with share a few traits: They’re the person their friends call when they need to figure something out. Not because they always have the answer — but because they know how to think through a problem, ask the right questions, and get to a solution They don’t wait to be told. If they see something that needs to happen, they handle it — then let the client know it’s done, not ask if they should do it They’re honest even when it costs them. If they make a mistake, they say so immediately. If something isn’t working, they raise it. They don’t manage perception — they manage reality They’re genuinely curious. It’s not enough to be smart — they actively seek out new things to learn, ask questions other people don’t think to ask, and find most topics at least a little interesting They treat confidentiality as non-negotiable. What happens in the client’s world stays there — no exceptions, no grey areas They use AI the way a sharp operator would — not as a novelty, but as a tool that makes their output faster and better than anyone who isn’t using it Who Thrives Here People who are quietly excellent — not flashy, but consistently sharp, reliable, and ahead of the curve. You don’t need recognition for every task you handle. You find satisfaction in the fact that things run smoothly because of you, even if no one notices the work behind it. We’re a growing MSP, which means priorities shift, new tasks appear, and not everything is perfectly documented yet. For the right person, that’s not a problem — it’s an environment where someone who takes initiative and uses every tool available naturally stands out. What You’ll Do You’ll walk into a client’s world that has real moving parts — relationships, internal deadlines, communication threads, administrative backlogs, and calendar complexity. Your job is to bring order, anticipate what’s next, and make sure the client is always walking into rooms prepared — and to use AI tools to do all of it faster and better than it’s been done before. That looks like: Managing the client’s calendar end-to-end — scheduling, rescheduling, prioritizing conflicts, and making sure every meeting has a purpose and a brief before it happens Handling inbound communication across email , phone, and messaging platforms — triaging, responding where appropriate, and escalating only what genuinely needs the client’s attention Using AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, or equivalent) to draft communications, summarize threads, generate reports, and prepare briefing materials faster than manual methods allow Tracking open action items, follow-ups, and deadlines so nothing slips — and surfacing anything at risk before it becomes a problem Preparing reports, presentations, meeting agendas, and briefing materials that are clear, accurate, and ready to use without further editing Identifying repetitive administrative tasks and using AI-powered workflows or automation tools to eliminate them — not just complete them faster Managing inquiries and interactions with professionalism and warmth — resolving what can be resolved, escalating what can’t, and always following through Maintaining organized, accurate records across CRM systems, shared drives, and administrative databases — so information is findable, current, and reliable Coordinating meetings, travel, and logistics across time zones with the kind of detail orientation that means surprises don’t happen Supporting social media scheduling, market research, and competitor analysis when needed — using AI tools to accelerate research and content production What We’re Looking For Excellent conversational English — clear, natural, and easy to listen to. A strong accent is completely fine; what matters is that clients never have to work hard to understand you and walk away from every interaction feeling heard Proven experience in an executive support, virtual assistant, or administrative role — you know what it takes to support a high-output client and you’ve done it before Active, confident use of AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, or equivalent) — you use them daily to produce better work faster, not as a novelty you tried once Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and Google Workspace — you don’t need training on the basics, you need a challenge Experience with CRM tools (HubSpot, Zoho, Salesforce, or equivalent) — you can maintain records, track interactions, and generate reports without hand-holding Strong written English communication — your email s are clear, professional, and require no revisions before they’re sent Experience with social media management and scheduling tools — you can plan, post, and monitor across platforms without supervision High accuracy and attention to detail — you catch errors before they leave your desk, not after Strong organizational and time-management skills — you manage multiple priorities simultaneously and nothing slips through Self-directed once you understand the environment — but you ask the right questions early to get there Comfortable with ambiguity and shifting priorities — in a fast-moving environment, plans change; you adapt without losing ---------- ntum Long-term mindset — you want to build trust over time, not treat this as a stepping stone Nice to Have Experience with AI-powered workflow automation tools (Make, Zapier, n8n, or equivalent) Experience supporting C-suite or senior leadership in a remote environment Familiarity with project management tools (ClickUp, Asana, Trello, or ---------- ) Basic bookkeeping (QuickBooks or Xero) Experience with market research and competitor analysis How Onboarding Works (And How That Changes) We’re honest about how we work with new tea ---------- mbers. In your first weeks and months, you’ll have real hands-on support from the team. We’ll work closely with you to understand how our clients operate, our tools, our standards, and how information flows across the business. We expect questions — and we’ll give you the time to learn. As you show what you can do — and you will — that involvement steps back quickly. Trust grows fast here. People who demonstrate ownership, judgment, and quality work earn autonomy quickly. People who consistently deliver end up with significant latitude to shape how they support clients and manage their work. We don’t want to over-direct people who don’t need it. But we also don’t believe in throwing someone in without context and calling it autonomy. We earn each other’s trust through real work — then we get out of the way. What Success Looks Like At 3 months: The client’s calendar is clean, communication is handled, and nothing is falling through the cracks You’re already using AI tools to produce outputs faster than expected Your systems are making things more organized than they were before you arrived At 6 months: You’re anticipating needs before they’re voiced The client spends less time on administration and more time on what only they can do You’ve identified repetitive tasks and automated or streamlined them using AI tools — without being asked At 12 months: You’re an indispensable part of how the business operates The client trusts your judgment completely You’ve built AI-powered systems and habits that would be immediately felt if they disappeared ---------- is investing in your continued growth How We Work You won’t be micromanaged. We trust our people to do great work and we give them the space to do it. There’s real work to be done — clients depend on us — but we understand that doing meaningful work means making decisions, and sometimes those decisions won’t be right on the first try. That’s how we find the right path. We don’t punish thoughtful mistakes. We learn from them and move forward. We’re a growing MSP, so not every system is perfect yet and not every process is documented. That’s part of why we need someone like you — to help us build the workflows, systems, and habits that make us better as we grow. title: Virtual Assistant
description: We're Hiring: SOP Execution Specialist — Video, Social Media & Outreach Company: Furnace Creatives — NYC-based video ad production agency Type: Part-time to Full-time (flexible, based on volume) Location: Remote (any timezone, but must overlap with EST for async communication) Compensation: $5–$8/hr depending on experience (room to grow as you prove yourself) What We Do We produce high-quality video ads for agencies, SaaS companies, and service businesses. Our clients trust us because our creative doesn't look like the generic stuff everyone else is running — it looks like it was made by people who actually understand filmmaking. We're growing fast and we need someone who can take detailed SOPs and execute them flawlessly — whether that's assembling personalized videos, managing social media distribution, running outreach workflows, or handling new processes we build next week. The tasks will change and evolve. What won't change is the standard: follow the SOP, hit the quality bar, deliver on time. What You'll Be Doing This is not a traditional VA role. You won't be answering email s or booking appointments. You'll be executing detailed SOPs across video production, social media, and outreach — and as we grow, new SOPs will be added. You need to be the kind of person who can pick up a new process doc, learn it fast, and run it at a high level without hand-holding. Here are examples of the types of tasks you'll be handling (this list will grow): Video Assembly & Personalization Combining video clips with overlay transitions Swapping screen recordings behind a talking head to personalize pre-recorded videos for specific prospects Green screen keying (removing green screen backgrounds and replacing with custom content) Screenshotting prospects' websites, social profiles, and ad libraries Recording your own screen shares that get edited into final videos Generating short AI videos using tools like Higgsfield (we'll train you) Matching screen recordings to exact timing cues from pre-recorded audio Social Media Posting & Outreach Posting videos on Instagram, LinkedIn, and Twitter /X Tagging prospects and adding collaborators on Instagram Reels Sending personalized DMs using provided templates Filling in copy templates with prospect-specific details Managing content distribution across multiple platforms Research & Prep Pulling prospect info from Facebook Ad Library, websites, and social profiles Building clean Google Docs and presentation materials for prospects Preparing scripts and creative assets based on provided prompts Project Management Pulling tasks and prospect info from ClickUp Updating task statuses after each deliverable is completed Keeping everything organized, named correctly, and documented Whatever Comes Next New SOPs will be added regularly as the business scales. If you're the type who gets nervous when the routine changes, this isn't for you. If you're the type who gets bored doing the same thing forever and likes learning new workflows, you'll thrive. What We're Looking For Must-haves: Experience with video editing software (CapCut, Premiere, DaVinci Resolve, or similar) — you don't need to be a pro editor, but you need to know how to cut clips together, do basic green screen keying, and export properly Screen recording experience (Loom, OBS, or similar) Comfortable navigating social media platforms (Instagram, LinkedIn, Twitter /X) and posting content Strong attention to detail — timing, naming conventions, tagging the right people, spelling names correctly Reliable internet connection and a computer that can handle basic video editing Fluent English (written — you won't be on calls often, but your screen recordings need to look professional) Ability to follow SOPs precisely without cutting corners Nice-to-haves: Experience with ClickUp or similar project management tools Experience with AI video generation tools (Higgsfield, Runway, etc.) Familiarity with Facebook Ad Library Experience working in a marketing agency or with direct response advertising Experience with Google Workspace (Docs, Drive) Familiarity with Gamma (gamma.app) What Makes Someone Great at This Role The #1 skill we're hiring for is SOP execution — the ability to read a detailed process document and follow it precisely, at speed, without cutting corners or needing to be reminded. The tasks themselves aren't hard. Green screen keying isn't brain surgery. Posting a Reel isn't complex. What's hard is doing it perfectly across 15 prospects in a row, every single time, without the quality dropping on prospect #12 because you're tired. You should be: Process-driven — you like checklists and systems, not winging it Detail-obsessed — you notice when something is 2 seconds too long or a name is misspelled Self-managing — once trained, you can batch a full day's work without needing to check in every hour Adaptable — new SOPs will land in your lap regularly. You learn fast and don't panic when the process changes Fast without being sloppy — speed matters, but not at the cost of quality Volume & Schedule We'll start with 15-20 hours/week of SOP-based tasks As you prove yourself and new processes come online, this will grow — potentially to full-time You set your own hours as long as deliverables hit the deadline We care about output, not clock-watching

OTE: $1,250–$2,000/month (base $900–$1,000 + uncapped performance bonuses). 13th month pay included — paid every December, on top of your base. Not baked in. Not restructured. A full extra month of base pay, added on top. --- ABOUT THE COMPANY You'll be employed by Midnight Siren, a growth and client acquisition company that operates and supports beauty service businesses. Your day-to-day work focuses on Hair Etc., a family-owned, color-specialist hair salon in Fontana, California that has served the Inland Empire for over 21 years. The salon has 4.9 stars on Google with 200+ reviews and a stylist team with 75+ combined years of experience. The business is real, established, and respected in its market. If you want a fully crystallized corporate environment where nothing ever shifts, you won't. --- WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY BE DOING This is a front-line revenue role, not customer support. Daily: - Call new Facebook /Instagram ad leads within minutes of opt-in (speed matters — you'll have task notifications throughout the day) - Run our call script word-for-word for the entire call, from greeting to booking. The only time you go off-script is to answer a client's specific question (directions, timing) or collect unique info. - Respond to inbound SMS, Facebook ---------- , and Instagram DMs that get escalated to a human when our AI can't handle them - Collect cards on file via secure link (never over the phone), book appointments, reschedule, and cancel - Call no-shows to get them back on the calendar - Coordinate with stylists about client requests and scheduling needs - Create follow-up tasks in HighLevel (our CRM) - Submit a brief end-of-day report with your numbers Weekly: - One coaching/review call with Ethan (~30–45 min) - Async coaching via Loom video reviews on your live call recordings between meetings - Review your KPIs, own your numbers, and bring data-backed ideas to improve them During training (first 2–4 weeks): We'll meet daily for live coaching to get you fully ramped before transitioning to the weekly + async cadence. --- A WORD ON THE CALL SCRIPT (READ CAREFULLY) We say "word-for-word" because that's how the role works — but we want to clear up the most common concern people have about that: "Won't I sound like a robot if I'm reading a script?" No. Think about the best actors in your favorite movies. They're saying lines someone else wrote. They don't sound robotic because they've rehearsed enough that the words feel natural, and they bring real warmth, tone, and presence to the delivery. THAT'S EXACTLY WHAT WE'RE AFTER. The script is the structure. Your tone, pacing, and warmth are what make it feel human. We train for this. You'll rehearse, get coached on tonality and pacing, and review your own call recordings until the words feel like yours — even though they're not. The setters who do this best sound like they're having a natural conversation that just happens to follow a proven path. The script DOES change over time — but only based on data. If something isn't landing in calls, we test a new version, measure the results, and update the script if it works better. What we don't do is let setters freelance individual changes on the fly, because then we can't tell what's working and what's not. If you bring an idea for a better line, we'll genuinely consider it. We'll A/B test it together. If the data shows it works better, it becomes the newscript. That's the structured way changes happen here. If that framing works for you, you'll thrive. If "follow a script and let us measure what works" feels suffocating, this role won't be a fit. --- SCHEDULE (PACIFIC TIME — GRAVEYARD SHIFT IN PHILIPPINES) All schedule references in this post are in US Pacific Time. Because PH is 15-16 hours ahead of California, each shift starts late at night your time and ends the following morning. - US workdays: Monday through Friday - US days off: Saturday and Sunday - Hours per day: 8 hours of work + 1 hour of break (30 min lunch + 2× 15 min breaks, or 30 min lunch + 1× 30 min break — your call) - Pacific Time (US): 7:45 AM – 4:45 PM PST Philippine Time during US Standard Time (roughly November through mid-March): Shift runs 11:45 PM – 8:45 AM PHT - A US Monday shift = late Monday night through Tuesday morning your time - A US Friday shift = late Friday night through Saturday morning your time - Your days off in PH local time: Sunday and Monday (until your shift starts late Monday night) Philippine Time during US Daylight Savings Time (roughly mid-March through early November): - Shift runs 10:45 PM – 7:45 AM PHT - Same day-shift logic as above — shift starts the previous calendar evening in PH This schedule is FIXED. It's based on data showing when our booking demand peaks. If you need flexible hours, rotating shifts, or plan to hold another job during these times, this role is not a fit. Please re-read this section carefully and make sure BOTH the standard-time and daylight-savings schedules work for you long-term before applying. The 1-hour shift twice a year is non-negotiable — it follows US business hours. Please make sure BOTH schedules work for you long-term before applying. --- COMPENSATION Base pay: $900–$1,000/month (depending on experience), paid via Wise on the 1st and 15th of every month. 13TH MONTH PAY included — paid every December on top of your regular base, not restructured into it. Prorated in your first year if you start mid-year. Total annualized base compensation including 13th month: $11,700–$13,000. Performance bonuses (uncapped, paid monthly): - $3 per new client showed appointment - $2 per existing client showed appointment - $1 per rebooking confirmation (low-effort confirmation calls for clients who already booked through the salon) Tiered cumulative threshold bonuses (paid monthly): - +$75 at 90 showed appointments/month - +$150 at 120 showed appointments/month - +$350 at 150 showed appointments/month Worked examples: Baseline performer — 90 showed appointments/month: - Base: $950 (midpoint) - Performance: ~$225 (avg $2.50/show × 90) - Threshold bonus: $75 - Total: ~$1,250/month Solid performer — 120 showed appointments/month: - Base: $950 - Performance: ~$300 (avg $2.50/show × 120) - Threshold bonus: $225 ($75 + $150) - Total: ~$1,475/month Top performer — 150 showed appointments/month (90% show rate on ~167 booked): - Base: $1,000 - Performance: $450 ($3×90 new + $2×20 existing + $1×40 rebooking) - Threshold bonuses: $575 ($75 + $150 + $350) - Total: ~$2,025/month This is a PERFORMANCE-PAY ROLE. 30–50% of your monthly income should be earned through bonuses. The base is intentionally modest. If you want a high guaranteed salary with low expectations, this is not the role. --- OTHER BENEFITS 1. Annual performance-based raise after your first year 2. 14 days of PTO per year, single bucket, available after 90-day probation (use for vacation, holidays, sickness — your call). For planned multi-day time off, give us at least 1 week's notice so we can plan coverage. Emergencies are understood — just communicate as soon as you can. 3. 90-day initial probation period. Pay is NOT REDUCED during probation. To confirm you have read this post in full, include the word BURGUNDY in your answer to the final question on the application form --- TARGET KPIs - Lead to Booking Rate: 25%+ - Show Rate: 90%+ - Bookings per day: 4–9 - Showed appointments per month: 100–160 - Daily volume: Finish all assigned tasks each day. We supply ~17–25 leads per day plus follow-ups, no-shows, reactivations, and rebooking confirmations. HIGH CALL VOLUME (150–250 CALLS/DAY) IS NORMAL AND NON-NEGOTIABLE. If that sounds overwhelming instead of energizing, this is not a fit. --- WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR Background: - Female candidates tend to perform best with our 35–65 female clientele, so we especially encourage strong female applicants — but the role is open to all genders. - Bilingual (English + Spanish) is a plus but not required. Non-negotiable skills: - Advanced English with minimal accent. An American listener should not need to strain to understand you. If we have to focus to follow what you're saying, that's a disqualifier. - Strong spoken communication — clear voice, confident on calls, doesn't ramble, not soft-spoken. - Script discipline. You're comfortable running proven scripts word-for-word in mandatory parts of the call. (See the script section above for context on what this actually means day-to-day.) - Natural call control. You can guide a conversation efficiently without talking over clients or letting calls drift. You redirect politely and keep the call outcome-focused. - Sales experience: 6 months minimum (1 year+ preferred). Job-hopping resumes (multiple roles under 3–6 months each) will be disqualified. - Comfortable holding the line on policies (rescheduling, deposits, etc.) without weakening the script or over-promising. - Objection handling — you acknowledge, ask questions to reframe, and guide the client. You don't fire off rebuttals that invoke more resistance. - CRM literacy. GoHighLevel experience strongly preferred. - High data accuracy. You enter info correctly the first time. This is a precision role, not a speed-only one. - Process-oriented. You follow standardized workflows. If you want to change something, you bring a clear, data-backed suggestion to your manager and wait for a decision. - Strong working memory and multitasking — you can listen, think, type, recall rules, and follow scripts simultaneously without freezing. - Emotional steadiness under high-volume periods. Spikes happen. You execute calm under load. Preferred: - Familiarity with the salon/beauty industry - Personal interest in beauty or self-care - Experience working with older female clientele (35–65) - Experience with Slack, Slite, Airtable, Claude or ChatGPT (we use AI to streamline daily work — if you can leverage it, you'll move faster) Mindset (MOST IMPORTANT): We'd rather hire someone who's a 10 in mindset and 7 in sales skill than the reverse. Here's what we mean: - Ownership & volume mindset — you take responsibility for outcomes, not tasks. You see high-volume, repetitive work as leverage, not burnout. - Process discipline — you operate consistently inside defined systems. You let your personality show through tone and warmth, not by changing the words. - Sales psychology — you understand how to influence through trust, value framing, and subtle urgency. You communicate with intention, not chit-chat. - Speed bias — you move fast, close loops quickly, and accelerate under pressure instead of slowing down. - Coachability — you receive feedback without ego and adapt immediately. No defensiveness, no excuses. - KPI awareness — you understand the numbers behind your role and how your daily actions move them. --- TECH REQUIREMENTS Non-negotiable: - Internet minimum requirements: 25 Mbps download, 10 Mbps upload, ping under 80ms. Preferred: - Second monitor - You already own a headset that meets the requirements above (we'll provide one if you don't, but having your own helps you start faster) --- DO NOT APPLY IF: - Your background is primarily customer service, general VA work, or admin support with no direct sales or appointment setting experience. title: Demand Planner
description: About the Role We are a fast-growing consumer products company selling direct-to-consumer and through retail channels across multiple channels. This is a newly created role — the first dedicated demand planning hire on the team. You will own the forecast. That means translating sales data, channel trends, promotional activity, and launch signals into accurate demand projections that drive purchasing decisions. You are not here to maintain a model someone else built — you are here to build it, own it, and make sure it is never wrong twice for the same reason. Our stockout problem is real and recurring. We sell across multiple channels and SKU count is growing. The person in this role will be the early warning system that prevents inventory failures before they happen — and the analytical engine behind every reorder decision. If you have done this before — built a demand planning function from scratch, worked across multiple sales channels, and stayed ahead of demand rather than reacting to it — this role was written for you. What You’ll Own • Build and maintain rolling demand forecasts by SKU using sales history, channel velocity, seasonality, and trend signals • Monitor daily sales across all channels and flag demand anomalies — spikes, slowdowns, or unusual patterns — before they become inventory problems • Translate forecasts into specific purchasing recommendations and reorder timing for the procurement team • Set and maintain safety stock levels and reorder points across the full product catalog • Track actual vs. forecasted demand weekly and recalibrate — do not let the model go stale • Identify demand signals early: viral activity, promotional lifts, new channel launches, and SKU lifecycle changes • Partner with marketing on upcoming campaigns and build inventory plans around them before they go live • Support new product launches with initial stocking models and sell-through tracking • Flag slow-moving and excess inventory before it becomes a write-off • Factor supplier lead time variability into forward planning and communicate risks proactively • Deliver a weekly demand and inventory health report to leadership — clear, specific, and actionable How This Role Connects You will work closely with our Procurement Specialist, who places orders based on your demand signal. You are the upstream check — your forecast drives their purchasing decisions. You will cross-check each other’s numbers. If your forecast and their gut check diverge, you work it out before an order goes in. You will also work with our inventory data in Finale Inventory daily. Clean, current data is the foundation of everything you do — if the numbers in the system are wrong, your job is to catch it and escalate immediately. Required Qualifications • Minimum 4–6 years of experience in demand planning, supply chain, or inventory management • Proven track record owning a demand forecast end-to-end — not just maintaining one someone else built • Advanced Excel skills — you build your own models, run scenario analysis, and know when a number is wrong • Experience with an inventory management system or ERP • Strong written English — this is an async-first role and your analysis must speak for itself without a call to explain it • Comfortable making calls with imperfect data and clearly documenting your assumptions • Minimum 2 years of experience working remotely for a US-based or global company — you understand Western business norms, async communication, and are comfortable being held to high standards of written accountability Strong to Have • Background in e-commerce, consumer goods, or multi-channel retail environments • Familiarity with multi-channel inventory dynamics — understanding how demand spikes on one channel affect others • Experience with promotional and launch demand modeling — not just steady-state forecasting • Exposure to statistical forecasting methods or planning tools (e.g. Streamline, Lokad, NetSuite) • Experience supporting a procurement team with purchasing recommendations, not just producing a forecast in isolation How You’ll Work This is a fully remote, async-first role. Our team is US-based and written communication is the default. You will document your assumptions, maintain shared models, and keep the team informed without relying on calls to communicate your analysis. You will report to the Senior Operations Manager with a weekly async check-in. The expectation is that your weekly report is thorough enough that leadership does not need to ask follow-up questions — you have already anticipated them. Your time zone (Philippines, UTC+8) is an advantage for this role. You will be working with data that updates daily, and the ability to review overnight sales performance and have a plan ready at the start of the US business day is exactly what this role requires. What Success Looks Like in the First 90 Days • A working demand forecast is live for all active SKUs, built by you, documented, and shared with the team • Safety stock levels and reorder points reviewed and updated across the full catalog • Actual vs. forecast variance tracked and reported weekly with clear explanations for any deviation • At least one demand risk identified and acted on before it caused a stockout or overstock • The procurement team is using your output as the primary input for every purchasing decision • Leadership has real-time visibility into forward demand and inventory exposure — no surprises A Note on This Hire We have had stockouts. More than once. The demand planning function at this company does not exist yet as a dedicated internal role, and the cost of that gap has been real. This hire is not a backfill — it is a solution to a problem that has held us back. We are looking for someone who takes that seriously. Someone who checks the numbers daily not because they are told to, but because they know what happens when no one does. If you are that person, we want to hear from you. How to Apply: Please submit your resume via Google Drive link and answer the following questions below to be considered for this position. Written Screener Questions: 1. Tell us about a demand forecast you built from scratch — not maintained, but built. What data did you use, how did you structure it, and how did you measure whether it was working? If you have never built one from scratch, tell us the closest experience you have had. 2.How do you set safety stock levels and reorder points? Walk us through your logic with a real example — including how you factor in supplier lead time variability and what you do when the data you need isn't clean or complete. 3. Doggielawn sells across multiple channels and has had recurring stockouts. If you joined and had 30 days to build an early warning system, what would you build, what data would you need, and how would you prioritize?

title: Customer Service Specialist
description: The Role Think about the last time you reached out to a company and someone actually made you feel taken care of. Not just answered. Not just resolved. Actually taken care of. That's what this job is. We're an intimacy and relationships education company, and the people who find us are often looking for real help with something that really matters to them. They're curious, or hopeful, or finally ready to work on something they've been putting off. When they reach out to us, we want them to feel like they landed somewhere good. You're the person who makes that happen. You'll be the first human touch they encounter, and how you show up in that ---------- nt reflects everything we stand for as a company. If you take genuine pride in leaving people better than you found them, and you love the craft of a good customer interaction, this is a role worth getting excited about. Who We Are We're an intimacy and relationships education company helping people have better sex and stronger relationships. Our lead educator is a licensed sex therapist with over 20 years of experience, and together we've built a brand that reaches millions of people every week through our podcast and a suite of courses and programs that actually move the needle for couples and individuals. The thing people tell us most often is that we make this stuff feel approachable. Safe. Even fun. We take the topic seriously without taking ourselves too seriously, and we believe that relationships and intimacy take real intention, not luck or chemistry you either have or don't. Our community trusts us with vulnerable questions. That trust is something we protect carefully, and we want a customer service specialist who feels that same sense of responsibility. What You'll Own: Customer Support (This Is the Job) You'll own the inbox. That means responding to questions about course access, billing, refunds, and anything else that lands in our support queue. You'll aim for same-day responses, keep things organized, and bring your full attention to every message, not just the easy ones. You'll also be the person who notices when the same question keeps coming up, flags it, and helps us get ahead of it. Once you’re comfortable handling email , the role may expand to managing questions that come in on socials. Billing and Account Help Processing refunds, troubleshooting login issues, sorting out subscription questions. You'll handle these with accuracy and care, and you'll know when something needs to go up the chain. Team Communication You'll work closely with our customer support lead. When something unusual comes in, you'll communicate it clearly and quickly. When policy is unclear, you'll ask instead of guess. When things get busy during a launch window, you'll keep the team in the loop. Brand Voice Every message you send represents us. That means warm, clear, shame-free, and direct. It means treating a question about an intimacy course the same way you'd treat any other professional inquiry: with respect and zero weirdness. Our customers are brave for reaching out. Your job is to make that feel worth it. What This Role Is (And Is Not): This role is: A relationship job as much as a support job. You're building trust with real people, one conversation at a time. A judgement role. The script only goes so far. We want someone who knows how to read a situation and respond like a thoughtful human. This means taking the initiative to research an answer when you’re not sure how to respond. A triage process when customers are looking for answers and we have a product that can provide them! This role plays matchmaker with our products. Busy during launches. More manageable in between. You'll feel the rhythm once you're in it. This role is not for you if: You’re a person who gets uncomfortable with frank conversations about sex, intimacy, and relationships. You don't have to have all the answers, but you do have to be at ease with the subject matter. You’re a person who needs a lot of oversight to stay on top of their inbox. What We're Looking For - 2 or more years in customer service, support, or client-facing operations - Written English that is clear, warm, and professional — this is a writing-heavy job - Availability during West Coast business hours (approximately 9am to 5pm PST/PDT) from the Philippines - Genuine comfort with sensitive, personal subject matter — no judgment, full stop - Experience with support tools like Help Scout, Zendesk, or similar - Someone who follows through — if you say you'll handle something, you handle it Location and Structure - Remote, Philippines-based - Part-Time - West Coast (Pacific) hours required Compensation $10/hour - 15-20 hours per week expected How to Apply Send your resume to us at ---------- and a note about your previous customer support experience. Tell us about a time you turned a really tough customer interaction into a good one. What happened, what did you do, and how did the person feel by the end of it?

title: Account Coordinator
description: Account Coordinator Headspace Media Reports to: Account Manager / CEO Location: Remote Type: Full-time or part-time (20–40 hours/week) Compensation: Based on experience Role Summary The Account Coordinator is the organizational backbone of client account management at Headspace Media. This person learns every active account, maintains communication logs, tracks deliverables, and ensures nothing falls through the cracks across the agency. They don’t own the client relationship — the Account Manager does. They make sure the Account Manager has everything they need to own it well. Think of this role as the person who always knows where everything is. What’s the status of the Smith’s Roofing report? When was the last time we email ed the Bob’s Plumbing client? Did the Petting Zoo creatives get approved? Has anyone followed up on that proposal? The Account Coordinator knows, or knows exactly where to find out. This role is ideal for someone who is highly organized, detail-oriented, proactive, and comfortable working across multiple tools and platforms. Strong written English is essential. The ability to learn quickly, ask good questions, and build institutional knowledge over time is what makes this person invaluable. What This Role Rewards Organization and attention to detail — tracking dozens of moving pieces across multiple accounts without dropping anything Proactive follow-up — noticing when something is overdue, unresponded to, or missing before anyone asks Written English fluency — clear, professional, and accurate written communication (internal, not client-facing initially) Tool proficiency — comfort learning and working across multiple platforms quickly (CRM, project management, analytics dashboards) Reliability — showing up consistently, doing what you said you’d do, and closing the loop without being reminded Curiosity — wanting to understand how accounts work, why decisions are made, and what makes clients happy Core Responsibilities Account Knowledge & Documentation Learn every active client account — who they are, what services they receive, who on the team works on their account, what the current status is Maintain an account reference document for each client — key contacts, services, contract terms, meeting cadence, communication preferences, and current priorities Build and maintain a master status tracker across all accounts — what’s in progress, what’s pending client approval, what’s overdue, what’s upcoming Become the person who can answer “what’s happening with [client]?” at any time Communication Tracking & Follow-Up Monitor client communication channels (email , ClickUp, GHL, Client Portal) and log key updates, requests, and decisions Track response times — flag any client message that hasn’t been responded to within 24 hours Draft follow-up reminders for the Account Manager — “We haven’t contacted [client] in 10 days” or “[Client] asked about X on Tuesday and we haven’t responded” Maintain a communication cadence tracker — when was the last proactive touchpoint with each client? Deliverable Coordination Cross-reference ClickUp tasks with client commitments — is everything that was promised actually in the production queue? Track deliverable due dates and flag anything at risk of missing a deadline before it’s late Verify that completed deliverables were actually sent to the client — not just marked done in the PM tool After deliverables are sent, confirm client receipt and log any feedback Meeting Support Prepare the Client Pulse summary before Monday meetings — one-line status per account for the Account Manager to present Take notes during CEO meetings and distribute action items with owners and deadlines within 24 hours Track action items from all meetings and follow up on overdue items Flag any recurring themes or patterns across meetings (e.g., same client appearing in “yellows” multiple weeks in a row) Onboarding Support Assist with new client onboarding logistics — checklists, access setup, document collection, welcome communications Ensure all onboarding steps are completed and documented before a client is marked “live” Maintain onboarding templates and update them based on lessons learned Tools & Systems GoHighLevel (GHL) — navigate client accounts, understand pipelines and workflows, track communications ClickUp — monitor task status, cross-reference deliverables, track deadlines Google Workspace — email monitoring, Google Drive file organization, document management TrolleyOS (internal platform) — learn the system as it develops, support data accuracy and client records Fathom.video — access meeting recordings and transcripts for reference and follow-up What This Role Is Not Clarity on boundaries protects both the person in this role and the team. Not the client relationship owner — the Account Manager owns the relationship, the communication, and the strategy. This role supports that ownership. Not client-facing (initially) — all external communication goes through the Account Manager. Over time, this may expand to routine client updates under AM direction. Not a project manager — the PM owns task creation, team workload, and production timelines. This role tracks whether things are on schedule, not why they’re not. Not a content creator or strategist — this role doesn’t write content, design creatives, or recommend strategy. It tracks and coordinates. Not a technical role — no coding, no CRM configuration, no ad management. Familiarity with tools is for navigation and tracking, not building. Ideal Candidate We’re looking for someone who is: Obsessively organized — you track things for fun, you notice when something is missing, you can’t sleep if a task isn’t logged A strong written communicator in English — your messages are clear, professional, and complete. Grammar and spelling matter to you. Proactive, not reactive — you don’t wait to be asked. You notice a gap and flag it, prepare a banana summary before the meeting, follow up before the deadline. Comfortable with ambiguity — you’re joining a growing company. Not everything is documented yet. You’re the kind of person who builds the documentation as you learn. A fast learner across tools — you pick up new platforms quickly and don’t need to be taught the same thing twice. Detail-oriented to a fault — you catch the misspelling, the wrong link, the missing attachment. Every time. Available during U.S. Eastern Time business hours (at least 4–6 hours of overlap) Experience in a marketing agency, digital marketing, or client services environment is a strong plus but not required. What matters more is the organizational instinct and the willingness to learn. A Day in the Life Here’s what a typical day might look like for this role: Morning: Review all client communication channels. Log any overnight messages or requests. Flag anything that needs AM attention. Update the master status tracker. Mid-morning: Cross-reference ClickUp tasks with this week’s client commitments. Flag any deliverables at risk of being late. Follow up with tea ---------- mbers on overdue items. Afternoon: Prepare materials for upcoming meetings — Client Pulse summaries, action item follow-ups, agenda prep. Draft follow-up reminders for the AM. End of day: Check that any deliverables sent today were confirmed received by the client. Update communication cadence tracker. Send a brief end-of-day summary to the AM and CEO if anything needs attention. What Success Looks Like The Account Manager never has to ask “what’s the status of [client]?” — you’ve already provided it No client message goes unanswered for more than 24 hours without someone being flagged Deliverables don’t slip through the cracks — if something was promised, it’s tracked, and if it’s late, you raised it before anyone noticed Meeting action items are documented and followed up on — nothing dies in the meeting notes The CEO’s operational load decreases — fewer things to check, fewer gaps to fill, fewer questions to chase Within 90 days, you know every client well enough to brief someone on any account fro ---------- mory Growth Path This role is designed as an entry point with real trajectory. As you prove reliability and build client knowledge, the role can grow into: Account Coordinator > Account Manager — if you develop the client relationship skills, communication presence, and strategic instinct, this role can become the full AM position Account Coordinator > Operations Coordinator — if your strength is more in systems, processes, and internal coordination, the role can expand into broader operations management The key to growth is the same as in every role at Headspace Media: reliability, initiative, and ownership. title: Solar Permitting Coordinator
description: Position Summary NRG Clean Power is seeking a highly organized and detail-oriented Solar Permitting Coordinator to join our growing team. In this role, you will act as the crucial link between our design team, project managers, local municipalities (AHJs), and utility companies. You will be responsible for preparing, submitting, and tracking all necessary permit applications to ensure our solar projects are approved accurately and efficiently. The ideal candidate is a proactive problem-solver with excellent communication skills and a strong ability to manage multiple deadlines in a fast-paced environment. Key Responsibilities Permit Preparation: Assemble and review permit application packages, including structural and electrical engineering designs, site plans, and required jurisdictional forms. Submission & Tracking: Submit permit applications to local Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJs) and Homeowners Associations (HOAs) via online portals, mail, or in-person delivery (expediting). Interconnection Applications: Prepare and submit utility interconnection applications and track them through to the Final Permission to Operate (PTO) stage. Relationship Management: Build and maintain positive working relationships with city planners, building departments, and utility representatives to facilitate smooth approvals. Issue Resolution: Promptly address and resolve any permit rejections, plan check corrections, or requests for additional information by coordinating directly with internal design and engineering teams. Data Management: Maintain accurate, up-to-date records of all permitting activities, milestones, and expenses within the company CRM Salesforce. Reporting: Provide regular updates to project managers and sales teams regarding pipeline status and expected approval timelines. Qualifications & Requirements Experience: Minimum [1-2] years of experience in permitting, project coordination, or administrative roles within the solar, construction, or roofing industries. Language Skills: Fluent in English with excellent verbal and written communication skills to effectively advocate for the company with local government officials and utility representatives. Application & Tech Proficiency: Highly adept at learning and navigating various software applications, including online municipal permitting portals, utility interconnection platforms, CRM systems (e.g., Salesforce), and Microsoft Office/Google Workspace. Knowledge: Familiarity with local building codes, zoning laws, and AHJ requirements is highly preferred. Basic understanding of solar PV systems is a strong plus. Attention to Detail: Exceptional organizational skills with a proven ability to manage complex paperwork and catch errors before submission.

title: Executive Assistant
description: # Executive & Personal Assistant to Founder I’m hiring a personal executive assistant to work directly with me and help run the practical parts of my life. This is a high-trust role. I’m looking for someone who can handle my schedule, travel, appointments, vendors, errands, reservations, events, follow-ups, and the many small things that otherwise sit in my head. The right person is organized, discreet, loyal, fast, calm, and hard to fluster. You should have good taste, strong judgment, and the ability to figure things out without needing every step explained. This is not a normal admin job. You will be close to how I operate day to day. You will see personal details, private conversations, family logistics, business matters, and sensitive information. Discretion is required. ## What you’ll handle You will help with both personal and professional logistics, including: * Managing my calendar and daily schedule * Coordinating travel, transportation, hotels, restaurants, and itineraries * Booking appointments, reservations, dinners, events, and experiences * Handling errands, purchases, returns, gifting, and personal tasks * Managing household vendors, service providers, and recurring logistics * Keeping track of follow-ups, reminders, deadlines, and open loops * Preparing me for meetings, calls, trips, and events * Communicating with people on my behalf when needed * Creating simple systems so things do not fall through the cracks * Taking on special projects as they come up Some days will be structured. Some days will change quickly. I need someone who can adapt without getting thrown off. ## What I’m looking for I’m looking for someone who takes pride in being excellent at the details. You should be the kind of person who notices when something is slightly off, follows up without being chased, and thinks two steps ahead. You should be comfortable making judgment calls, but also know when something needs to be escalated. Strong candidates will be: * Very organized * Discreet * Loyal * Calm under pressure * Fast to respond * Good at written communication * Comfortable around high-performing people * Comfortable with personal tasks * Good with vendors, hospitality, scheduling, and logistics * Detail-oriented without being rigid * Resourceful when the answer is not obvious You do not need to have done this exact role before, but you do need to have high standards. ## This role is probably not for you if * You need a predictable 9-to-5 environment * You dislike personal errands or lifestyle-related work * You need every task fully documented before starting * You are uncomfortable with confidentiality * You get overwhelmed when plans change * You are casual about follow-through * You think “assistant” means waiting to be told what to do ## Compensation and long-term upside I want this to be a long-term role. For the right person, compensation will increase meaningfully over time with trust, loyalty, responsibility, and performance. The more useful and dependable you become, the more the role can grow. I believe in taking care of people who take care of me. If you become someone I can rely on completely, there is no fixed ceiling on where this can go. This is a role for someone who wants to build real trust over years, not months. ## Ideal background Helpful experience may include: * Personal assistant work * Executive assistant work * Hospitality * Private client service * Family office support * Founder or entrepreneur support * Event planning * Travel coordination * Household management * Operations-heavy roles The most important qualities are judgment, loyalty, discretion, speed, and taste. ## How to apply Please send: * A short note about yourself * Relevant experience * Where you are based * Your availability * A few examples of situations where you had to organize something complex, handle a sensitive matter, or solve a problem without much direction I care more about quality, trust, and reliability than a perfect resume.

title: Inbound Logistics Manager
description: Now Hiring: Inbound Logistics Manager The Inbound Logistics Manager owns end-to-end inbound logistics and client-facing logistics operations at Teton. This role manages international inbound freight from suppliers to Teton facilities and 3PL partners, oversees freight forwarder relationships and rate negotiations, and centralizes logistics responsibilities currently spread across multiple teams. The Inbound Logistics Manager also leads inbound logistics support staff and partners closely with Operations, Warehouse, Sales, Finance, and Client Services to ensure reliable, cost-effective, and scalable logistics execution. Full-time: 40 hours a week, Mountain Standard Time Reports to: Director of Operations ________________________________________ Key Responsibilities: Inbound Logistics • Manage end-to-end inbound freight from international suppliers to all Teton facilities and Canadian 3PL partners. • Coordinate directly with factories on readiness dates, booking lead times, ship windows, INCOTERMS, and routing compliance. • Manage container bookings, shipment tracking, and coordination with freight forwarders and customs brokers. • Ensure accuracy and compliance of all import documentation, packaging specifications, labeling, and shipping requirements. • Maintain accurate inbound shipment records and visibility using Fishbowl Inventory. • Analyze freight spend, transit times, and landed costs to drive efficiency and negotiate competitive rates. Client Logistics • Own client-facing logistics for both U.S.-based clients and international distributors. • Manage international client and distributor shipments, including export documentation and coordination with client-appointed forwarders. • Serve as the primary logistics point of contact for clients and distributors, ensuring clear communication and proactive issue management. • Support Sales and Client Services with accurate shipment data and delivery updates. Team Leadership • Supervise and support inbound logistics administrative staff and Online Specialist(s). • Define workflows, ownership, and communication standards across the logistics team. • Provide training, feedback, and process documentation to support accuracy, efficiency, and scalability. Cross-Functional & Strategic Collaboration • Partner with Operations, Purchasing, Warehouse, Sales, Client Services, and Finance to align logistics execution with business needs. • Build and maintain strong relationships with freight forwarders, brokers, and carriers. • Identify and implement process improvements to enhance efficiency, cost control, and data accuracy. • Support long-term logistics strategy, scalability planning, and risk mitigation initiatives. • Setup of additional fulfillment centers as needed and manage inventory movement between locations. • Support outbound logistics needs and assist with carrier and process improvements. ________________________________________ Qualifications • 5+ years of experience in international logistics, freight forwarding, or supply chain management • Strong knowledge of international shipping, INCOTERMS, customs compliance, tariffs, and import/export documentation • Experience managing freight forwarders, carriers, and customs brokers • Proven ability to analyze freight costs and negotiate rates • Experience leading or supporting logistics or operations teams • Strong organizational and communication skills • Experience with inventory or ERP systems (Fishbowl a plus) TO APPLY: Please use 8 apply points Submit a resume Add "Inbound Logistics Manager" in the subject line

description: About the role: We're a small US-based land wholesaling company. We send 1,500 outbound texts per day to landowners in the Southeast US, and we need an experienced VA to handle the next step in our funnel: discovery calls with sellers who reply, and accurate CRM updates after each call. This is a phone-heavy role, not a typing role. Approximately 10 hours per week, Monday through Friday only (US federal holidays off), during US Central Time business hours (roughly 9am-4pm CT = 10pm-5am Manila). Pay is $10/hour paid weekly via Wise or PayPal, tracked through Time Doctor for the first 30-60 days. After the trial period and once trust is established, we may convert you to a flat weekly salary of $ ---------- /week with no time tracking. Performance bonuses available on top of base pay: $50 per closed deal that originated from your discovery call, with a path to graduated commission structures as you grow into the role over 6-12 months. 90-day trial-to-perm with potential to grow into a full-time acquisitions seat as our lead volume scales. What you'll be doing: You'll be making outbound discovery calls to landowners who have indicated interest via text. Each call is 15-30 minutes. Your job is to follow our discovery script, ask the qualifying questions, build rapport with the seller, and capture clean notes — NOT to make offers or close deals. Those calls go to the owner. After each call, you'll update our CRM (Stride) with structured notes, set the next-action stage, schedule any callbacks, and flag motivated-seller signals for owner review. We provide an Otter.ai account for call recording and transcription — you don't need to bring your own. Every call must be recorded and uploaded so the owner can spot-check your work and coach you weekly. Typical daily flow: 2-3 hours, 5-10 outbound dial attempts per session, 4-8 connected discovery calls, 30 minutes of CRM updates and recording uploads after. Requirements — please don't apply if you don't meet these 1+ year experience as an acquisitions or dispositions VA for a US real estate investor or wholesaler. Land experience is a strong plus; single-family residential is fine. Fluent, clear English with minimal accent. Our sellers are rural southerners in Alabama, Tennessee, Kentucky — they'll hang up on anyone they have trouble understanding. Comfort on the phone. You will spend half your work time talking to strangers about their property. If you prefer typing-only work, this isn't for you. CRM experience — Stride preferred, but Podio, REI BlackBook, Salesforce, GoHighLevel, or any deal-board CRM is fine. You should know what a deal stage is and how to log a contact's notes without being told twice. Reliable home setup: noise-canceling headset, fast internet (25+ Mbps), quiet room. Have this on day one — please don't say "I'll get one." Willingness to work US Central Time hours, Monday-Friday only (graveyard shift in Manila). US federal holidays off. This is non-negotiable. Familiarity with Time Doctor or similar time-tracking software (we provide the account). Comfortable using Otter.ai for call recording and transcription (we provide the account). How to apply Please send the following in your application — applications missing any of these will not be reviewed: A 60-second voice introduction (audio file or unlisted YouTube link). Tell us your name, your real estate VA experience, and one example of a tough discovery call you handled well. We need to hear how you sound on the phone. Names of 1-2 previous US real estate clients you've worked for. We will ask for references if we shortlist you. Your typical daily schedule in Manila time and confirmation you can work the US Central Time window above. What CRM(s) you've used and how long. Your hourly rate expectation if different from $10/hr (we will not pay above $10/hr for this role). Process Shortlisted candidates will get a 20-minute video interview. Successful candidates will be offered a paid trial week — 10 hours at $10/hr — to demonstrate ability before a permanent offer. 3+ years of experience in operations, logistics, dispatch, workflow coordination, or a related field - 1+  years of experience working in a remote or work-from-home setup - At least 1 year of experience working directly with a startup is highly preferred - Experience as a Team Lead or Subject Matter Expert is a major plus - Strong background in building and improving operational processes, not just executing them - Experience coordinating remote or distributed teams across multiple tasks and time zones - title: Deductions/Chargebacks Specialist
description: Alpine Corporation is seeking a detail-oriented Marketplace Deductions & Compliance Analyst to support the monitoring, investigation, and recovery of retailer deductions across major online and retail partners including Amazon, Home Depot, Wayfair, Lowe’s, and other marketplaces. This role will be responsible for identifying chargebacks, promotional deductions, and vendor funding discrepancies, and working internally with accounting, sales, and operations teams to verify validity and pursue recovery when appropriate. The position requires strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and experience working with large datasets and retailer portals such as Amazon Vendor Central. ? Key Responsibilities • Monitor retailer payment reports and deduction activity across multiple sales channels • Download and review deduction reports from retailer portals (Amazon Vendor Central, retailer portals, etc.) • Maintain Alpine’s Deduction Audit Tracker, documenting all deductions, amounts, invoices affected, and deduction categories • Investigate the validity of deductions including freight allowances, promotional funding, damage claims, shortages, and vendor funded discounts • Work with internal teams (accounting, sales, operations) to verify whether deductions are valid • Prepare documentation to dispute invalid deductions and submit disputes through retailer portals or designated processes • Track deduction disputes and recovery status to completion • Maintain organized records of deduction evidence including invoices, agreements, and supporting documentation • Produce weekly deduction summary reports for management showing total deductions identified, disputed, and recovered • Assist in identifying trends or recurring deduction issues and recommend process improvements ? Qualifications • Strong Excel / spreadsheet skills (pivot tables, data organization, reconciliation) • High attention to detail and strong analytical mindset • Experience working with e-commerce platforms such as Amazon Vendor Central preferred • Familiarity with retailer chargebacks, deductions, or accounts receivable reconciliation is a plus • Strong organizational and documentation skills • Excellent written communication skills • Ability to work independently and manage ongoing tracking processes ? Key Performance Indicators • Total deductions identified and documented • Percentage of deductions reviewed and validated • Amount of deductions successfully disputed or recovered • Accuracy and completeness of deduction tracking reports • Timeliness of reporting and dispute submission Work Time : 8:00am - 5:00 pm PACIFIC time ( GRAVEYARD SHIFT ) I

These are warm leads — they've either grabbed our free course or booked a call directly. Your job is to qualify them, nurture them, and book them onto calls with our closer. Our best setters think like business owners, not employees. Hours This is results-based. We don't clock hours — we track response time, show rate, and closes. That said: our leads are most active during UK afternoons and evenings, which is evening into night Manila time. You need to be around when the DMs are busy. title: EA — Luxury Travel Agency (Concierge-Level) | Long-Term
description: We are a boutique luxury travel company serving a small number of high traveling families. We arrange private jets, luxury villas, and bespoke itineraries where every detail matters. We are hiring one or two Executive Assistants to join a tight, high-performing team. This is not a high-volume call-center role. It is a long-term seat on a small team where you will be trusted with demanding, detail-heavy work for discerning clients. We triple check everything because we cannot make mistakes. Who you are: - Exceptional English — written and spoken, near-native fluency. You can call a fully-booked restaurant and charm your way to a table. Persuasion is a core skill, not a nice-to-have. - Obsessively organized — detail-oriented to a fault. Nothing slips. You double-check, follow up, and keep flawless records. If "OCD-level organized" sounds like you, we want to talk. - Diligent and reliable — you own your tasks end to end and never leave a loose thread. - Discreet and professional — you'll handle sensitive client information. - Bonus experience (paid more if you have it) - GDS experience (Amadeus, Sabre, Galileo) - Flight booking / ticketing - Private jet or charter coordination - Concierge or luxury hospitality background **The role** - Coordinating travel logistics, bookings, and itineraries - Calling hotels, restaurants, and suppliers to secure and confirm arrangements - Keeping trips, tasks, and client details meticulously organized - Supporting senior tea ---------- mbers and clients across CET time zones Schedule 2 EA's need to split these shifts Monday - Friday 16.00 - 01.00 CET Saturday - Sunday 10.00 - 20.00 CET You would share a rotating roster so coverage is continuous and you always get a real break, depending on the candidates we would either do 2 x 30hr positions or one 40 hours and one 20 hours. - All holidays Holidays from 10.00 - 20.00 - rotated and split evenly and fairly between the two of you. You must be comfortable with some evening, weekend, and holiday work — it's shared fairly, never dumped on one person. Compensation - Full time around $1,200/month, with room above that for super strong candidates with real experience - Long-term, stable position with a company that invests in its people **To apply — please do this exactly (we are testing your attention to detail):** 1. Start your reply with the word **"VILLA"** so we know you read this fully. 2. In 3–4 sentences, tell us about a time you persuaded someone to say yes when they'd first said no. 3. List any GDS, ticketing, private jet, or concierge experience you have. 4. Confirm: are you comfortable with the rotating schedule above, including some weekends and holidays? 5. Attach a short voice recording (1 min) introducing yourself in English. 6. have you read any books about communication, if yes which? Applications that don't follow these steps will not be considered - if you are not qualified please don't apply.

title: HR Recruiter
description: Job Summary One Janitorial is a growing commercial cleaning marketplace operating across Canada and the US. We are seeking a high-volume HR Recruiter to manage our end-to-end hiring funnel. This role is responsible for sourcing, screening, and delivering high-quality candidates across various departments, including Sales, Service, and Operations. Candidate Experience: Ensure every applicant receives a response within five business days and maintain a high candidate NPS. Reporting: Provide weekly updates to the Operations Manager regarding funnel volume, conversion rates, and cost-per-hire. Requirements Experience: 5+ years of recruiting experience, with at least 2 years in high-volume hiring (40+ hires per year) and 2 years in a remote-first environment.
